notes: Bays back to canted three-sash bays (glass drums removed); warmer mustard ochre wall #b08a48; warm brown tile bulkheads with fine grout; cornice brackets smaller and further apart under the dentil course; bays bowed (roundCorners 3) and glazed with sash-bar panes (paneM 0.45) in white frames; partCornice deeper (1.6 m, proj 0.6) with smaller, closer paired brackets; floor stack 4.2 ground / 4.1 upper (~1:1 storeys, same 8.3 m); stucco repaint patches removed (even colour, only sill streaks and soot); sign fascias in varied deep tones (green, cream-edged dark, oxblood, navy) instead of four black boxes; interior: salon and bar rebuilt with fitted kits (unitKits19: mirrors at styling stations, basin, product shelves, reception; back bar with bottle shelves, stone counter, stools) and the plant/lounge-chair strays that rendered as floating shards removed; picture rails walnut not black. Data: spec/style keep 2 storeys + LiDAR 9.79 m; spec material stays as generated (painted stucco is the style wall). Tile pent lowered (rise 0.4 -> 0.26, bay 0.16); window frames and corner sashes white with the red kept on the surrounds and cornice (were solid red); fewer, irregular upper openings (two removed); a yellow awning on the middle shop and a deeper blue one; wider blade sign. Identity resolved against data: the DataSF footprint is ONE 21 m polygon and one assessor record, so the tile corner part and the bracketed-bay part both belong to this building (dossier line about a separate bay neighbour was wrong). Dark red sash frames with divided upper lights, a mullioned sash pair and curtains; upper-left volume reset to a single, a small balcony window and a wide sash pair with more plain wall; storefront doors in 1.0 m recessed entries with tiled floors and glazed returns; grout-lined tile bulkheads; bays project 0.8 m and stop lower under the frieze; heavier paired brackets; library furniture embedded in the fine storeys (the runtime ignores lib: empties); a rug in every flat. Floor stack 4.5 m ground / 3.8 m upper; two volumes along Castro: the corner-side ~46 % keeps the clay-tile pent roof, a plain wall and a thin band, the far ~54 % alone carries the bays under a deeper bracketed eave; rounded corner bay with more facets and tall arch-headed sashes under the wrapping tile eave; upper sashes shorter (sill 0.8, head 2.75) with darker room-tone backing (fewer pale blinds) so the white double-hung frames and meeting rails read; brighter green shopfront piers; divan base under every bed (no lifted mattress). Upper windows shorter and wider (sill 1.05, head 3.15 over the 4.2 upper storey, 1.2 m wide) under a deep plain frieze; the two Castro bays are lower (bayRoofDropM 0.55) and shallower so they sit under the frieze, not up into the roofline; the bracketed cornice is a deep plain frieze with one thin oxblood moulding and small paired brackets (pairGapM), no drop blocks, no dentils; the tile part (corner third + 17th face + corner bay) is a separate lower volume: tile lip 8.05 m and hipped rise, so the two-part composition reads; ground floor gets a tall black sign board per unit (boardM 1.0, head drop 1.25) with the awnings hung under the board; dark stone bulkheads; darker rooms and curtains behind the upper glass; corner door dark green; stronger weathering contrast. Interiors: oak/tile floors and a ceiling in every unit and flat, stools on the pizzeria counter, lounge corner in the bar, nightstand/lamp/frames/coffee table in the flats. Sill streaks, soot band under the cornice, faded repaint patches); raised barrel-tile rows on the pent and the corner-bay eave (tileBarrels) with a taller rise so the tile hip has relief; the two Castro bays are deeper canted three-sash bays (0.8 m, 2.9 m wide) under heavier scroll brackets with no dentil teeth; corner bay gets plain square-headed sashes; awnings over four of the five units, deep-red corner-bar door; deeper window surrounds; mixed room tones behind the glass (curtains and dark rooms, not uniform bright panes). Interiors: per-unit wall paint, wainscot and picture rail (unitDress), the units become a market, a hair salon, a pizzeria counter and the corner bar; flats get painted walls and a desk / armchair / dresser each (flatDress). Floor stack stays the photograph-fitted 4.1/4.2 (spec 5.97/3.22 is make-spec's heuristic, not a measurement. LiDAR 9.79 shellTop is the only measured height and still holds). Not fixable in this building: missing south neighbour, 17th St context, trolley wires. The kit's awning-canvas is a fixed red/cream stripe in the runtime (tint ignored), so both unit awnings went back to tinted painted-white; wall toned from #a88541 (read chrome-yellow in game) to #9a7a40. The tile corner part is now t 0.0.45 with only three irregular openings (a small high single, a single, one wide triple) instead of an even grid; the bracketed-cornice part t 0.45.1 reads window, balconette, canted three-light bay, a narrow sash, canted bay against the theatre (the bays no longer touch). Warmer saturated ochre wall. Tile pent faded red-brown (not salmon, not crimson) with a lower lip (8.8 m) so the slope reads as depth. Storefront: navy canvas awning and a mustard canvas awning on separate units, two blade signs, lighter stone bulkheads, glazed corner-bar entry on the chamfer (was a blank panel door). Corner bay: four wider facets so the windows read as tall round-headed sashes, not lancets. DATA RECONCILIATION: spec floors (ground 5.97 / upper 3.22) come from make-spec's civic tallGround heuristic, not a measurement; the only measured height is LiDAR shellTop 9.79 m, which the build still hits exactly. The Castro frontage is the spec frame width 20.84 m (earlier notes' '19 m' was the storefront run, not the lot). The exposed south return wall is the world gap W1 (the neighbouring two-storey Italianate is not built yet); in reality that neighbour abuts it. The 19 m Castro front is two frontages on one footprint - the corner part (edge 4, t 0.0.47 from the corner) keeps the clay-tile pent (weathered brown-red, lip 9.0 m, small rise) over the corner bay and the 17th face; the south part (t 0.47.1) gets two canted three-light bays on the upper storey under a flat bracketed cornice (partCornice) with a balconette and a single sash beside them; the cornice returns on the exposed south wall, which gets its own weathered render skin, flashing, plinth and downpipe (returnWall). Warmer ochre wall, near-black continuous sign fascias, cast-stone bulkheads, one navy awning, taller and wider upper sashes, floor stack 4.1/4.2, rounder six-facet corner bay. Thin low-pitch clay-tile pent (lip 9.30 m, no rise; ~0.5 m band, was ~2.3 m) over the slim dentil cornice; floor stack 4.3/3.9 so the belt and upper windows sit lower and the frieze reads slim; muted ochre wall; cornice and pent return onto the exposed south side wall; ground units cafe/cafe/fast-food/bar (no grocery shelving); upper storey as five small flats. Squat floor stack (ground 4.0 m, upper 3.7 m); tall sloped clay-tile band in two steps (higher corner section over 17th and the corner bay, lower run to the south) with tile courses, ridge roll and rafter tails; projecting cornice band with dentils under it; irregular upper openings (single double-hungs at uneven spacing, a wide triple window, a small balcony with a wrought-iron railing; two balconies on 17th) in heavy dark-red surrounds with moulded heads; wider four-facet corner bay with arched windows; per-unit shopfronts with separate sign boards, a yellow and a blue canvas awning, two blank blade signs, gooseneck lamps, brown tile bulkheads; house-number plaque, door lamp, conduit and meter box; float-finish stucco; a fast-food counter unit. Mission-revival clay-tile pent eave on both street faces and around the corner bay (tileEave); bowed corner bay across the chamfer with tall arch-headed windows (cornerBay); dark green storefront piers (storefrontPiers); denser taller upper windows; muted ochre wall with red trim; ground split into a corner bar, two small shops and a small cafe (groundUnits); upper storey as four small flats plus a hall off a rear corridor (upperFlats). 2-storey 1901 corner mixed-use, SE corner of Castro Street and 17th Street. Mustard-ochre smooth stucco, Mission-revival red clay-tile pent eave along both street faces, flat roof. Upper storey: irregular punched double-hung windows in white frames and a rounded corner bay with tall windows at the chamfer; 17th Street face two windows. Ground: continuous shopfronts with dark green piers and frames, dark sign fascia band over them, dark tile bulkheads, a corner bar glazed around the chamfer, a blue canvas awning mid-run, a stair door to the flats near the south end. Signage kind only.
